q: What may the selection committee do during the Verification step of Comparative Selection?
o: Issue the Terms of Reference
Conduct the final fee negotiation
Visit buildings designed by the Architects and check references such as former clients and financial institutions
Announce the winner of the design competition
n: Verification allows the selection committee to visit buildings designed by the Architects and check references, such as former clients and financial institutions. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.3.2.4 (Verification))

q: The SPP defines "Professional/s" as Registered and Licensed Professionals (RLPs). What distinguishes an RLP from an Architect under this definition?
o: An RLP is licensed by the DTI rather than the PRC
An RLP does not need a valid professional identification card
An RLP practices a State-regulated profession other than Architecture
An RLP is always a juridical person, never a natural person
n: Professional/s are defined as RLPs — natural persons with a valid certificate and identification card — for the lawful practice of a State-regulated profession other than Architecture. (Source: SPP Annex A, General Definitions, Item 8)

q: For what kind of projects is an Architectural Design Competition (ADC) typically used, and what are its possible formats?
o: Civic or monumental projects; it may be an idea competition, a design competition, or a design-build competition
Small residential renovations; it is always a design-build competition
Any project regardless of scale, replacing Direct and Comparative Selection entirely
Interior fit-out projects only; it is always an idea competition
n: An Architectural Design Competition (ADC) is used for civic or monumental projects, and may be an idea competition, a design competition, or a design-build competition. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.3.3)

q: Under the SPP, "Contractor" and "General Contractor" shall also mean which other terms?
o: Client or Owner
Professional or Consultant
Sponsor or Project Proponent
Constructor or Builder
n: The SPP states that Contractor and General Contractor shall also mean Constructor or Builder, and these terms may be used interchangeably. (Source: SPP Annex A, General Definitions, Item 10)

q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of an Architectural Design Competition (ADC) noted in the SPP?
o: It is limited only to foreign architects
The Client is barred from serving on the jury
It cannot be used for civic or monumental projects
The process may be expensive and time consuming, potentially discouraging qualified firms from participating
n: Disadvantages listed include that the process may be expensive and time consuming, and that the time and effort required may discourage qualified firms from participating. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.3.3.2)

q: The 2010 SPP is promulgated as Annex "A" of the IRR of which law, and what set of older documents does it replace?
o: R.A. No. 9266; it replaces the 2004 IRR in its entirety
R.A. No. 8981 (PRC Modernization Act); it replaces the 1979 UAP Docs. 101 through 109
The Civil Code of the Philippines; it replaces the 1979 National Building Code
R.A. No. 9266 (Architecture Act of 2004); it replaces the 1979 UAP Docs. 201 through 209
n: The 2010 SPP is promulgated as part of the IRR of R.A. No. 9266, the Architecture Act of 2004, and is to be known hereinafter as the SPP Documents, replacing the 1979 UAP Docs. 201 through 209. (Source: SPP Annex A, cover/title page)

q: Per the SPP's procedure for Architectural Design Competitions, competitions should be conducted with the assistance of which organization, and in accordance with what?
o: The Department of Labor and Employment, in accordance with the Labor Code
The Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA) or one of its local chapters, in accordance with the Architect's Guidelines
The Professional Regulation Commission, in accordance with R.A. No. 8981
The Department of Trade and Industry, in accordance with the National Building Code
n: Competitions should be conducted with the assistance of the IAPOA or one of its local chapters, and in accordance with the Architect's Guidelines. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.3.3.3 (Procedure))

q: What does the acronym ADR stand for in the SPP acronym list?
o: Architect's Design Requirements
Architectural Design Review
Annual Development Report
Alternative Dispute Resolution
n: ADR is defined in the SPP acronym list as Alternative Dispute Resolution. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. B (Acronyms))

q: A foreign architect wants to compete in a Philippine design-build architectural competition. Besides being registered in his own country, what must he additionally secure, and what must he do regarding a local counterpart?
o: Secure only a business permit from the DTI, with no need for a local counterpart
Obtain a certificate of registration from the SEC in lieu of a TSP

Secure a Temporary Special Permit (TSP) from the PRC and a work permit from the DoLE, and work in collaboration with a local/Filipino counterpart RLA who assumes the professional responsibilities and civil liabilities
Join IAPOA as a full voting member before competing
n: A foreign architect-competitor must be registered in his/her country of origin, secure a TSP from the Commission (PRC), obtain a work permit from the DoLE, and work in collaboration with a local/Filipino counterpart RLA who will assume the requisite professional responsibilities and civil liabilities in a design or design-build competition. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.3.3.4(b))

q: What does the acronym MoP refer to in the SPP?
o: Memorandum of Partnership
Ministry of Practice
Manual of Procedure
Method of Payment
n: MoP is listed in the SPP acronym section as Manual of Procedure. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. B (Acronyms))

q: What is the minimum number of jury members required for an Architectural Design Competition, and what qualities must they be known for?
o: At least ten (10) members appointed solely by the Commission
Exactly two (2) members, one from the Client and one from the Board
At least three (3) members, all of whom must be foreign architects
At least five (5) members known for their integrity, objectivity, impartiality, and honesty
n: The Jury must be composed of at least five (5) members known for their integrity, objectivity, impartiality, and honesty. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.3.3.4(d))

q: Section C of the 2010 SPP, "General Notes on the Selection of the Architect," is part of the IRR of R.A. No. 9266 and replaces which earlier document?
o: The 1979 UAP Doc. 209
The 1979 UAP Doc. 201
The 1979 UAP Doc. 208
n: Section C is expressly noted as being part of the IRR of R.A. No. 9266, replacing the 1979 UAP Doc. 208. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C heading)

q: Section C of the SPP closes with a short note on the 'Method of Compensation.' What does this section state?
o: A fixed percentage fee schedule applicable to all selection methods
That compensation must always be negotiated through IAPOA
That only Direct Selection engagements are compensated
That compensation will be covered by the respective type of services
n: Section C.4 simply states that the method of compensation will be covered by the respective type of services, without prescribing specific fee figures in this general section. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.4 (Method of Compensation))

q: Under Section C, what does the Scope of Services for an engagement depend on?
o: The Architect's professional identification card number
Whether the project is public or private
The number of competitors in an Architectural Design Competition
The method by which the Architect is selected
n: Section C.2 states that the scope of services will depend on the method by which the Architect is selected. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.2 (Scope of Services))

q: The Standards of Professional Practice (SPP) is a required document under which provision of law?
o: Sec. 14 of R.A. No. 9266
Sec. 37 of R.A. No. 9266
Sec. 41 of R.A. No. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004) and its IRR
R.A. No. 8981 (The PRC Modernization Act of 2000)
n: The SPP is expressly identified as a required document under Sec. 41 of R.A. No. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004) and its Implementing Rules and Regulations. (Source: SPP Annex A, General Definitions, Item 2)

q: Which of the following is NOT listed under Section C as a basis for Direct Selection of an Architect?
o: Recommendation of the architect's former client
The architect's reputation
Personal or business acquaintance, or recommendation of a friend
Winning an Architectural Design Competition
n: Direct Selection bases listed are reputation, personal/business acquaintance or a friend's recommendation, recommendation of a former client, and recommendation of another architect. Winning a design competition belongs to the separate ADC method, not Direct Selection. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.3.1)

q: The SPP defines "Board" as referring only to the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture (PRBoA). Under whose supervision and administrative control does the Board operate?
o: The Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects
The Department of Labor and Employment
The Commission (PRC)
The Department of Trade and Industry
n: The PRBoA is created under R.A. No. 9266 and its IRR, and operates under the supervision and administrative control of the Commission (PRC). (Source: SPP Annex A, General Definitions, Item 4)

q: In a Comparative Selection process, on what document is the Terms of Reference (ToR) issued to prospective architects based?
o: The Architect's Guidelines fee schedule
The Design Brief prepared by another Architect
The Client's building permit application
The winning entry from a prior Architectural Design Competition
n: In the Invitation step of Comparative Selection, the Client issues an invitation including the Terms of Reference (ToR), which is based on the Design Brief prepared by another Architect. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.3.2.1 (Invitation))

q: Depending on the specific SPP document, the term "Architect" may also refer to which of the following roles under R.A. No. 9266?
o: Architect-of-record (Aor), Architect in charge of construction (Aicc), or Consulting Architect (CA)
Contractor, Constructor, or Builder
Professional/s (RLPs)
Client, Owner, or Project Proponent
n: The definitions state that, depending on the SPP, Architect may also refer to Architect-of-record (Aor), Architect in charge of construction (Aicc), or Consulting Architect (CA), as provided under R.A. No. 9266. (Source: SPP Annex A, General Definitions, Item 5)

q: During the Interview step of a Comparative Selection process, what does the Architect do?
o: Submits a sealed bid amount
Explains his methodology in translating the plan/design requirements of the proposed project
Files a complaint before the Board
Presents a signed construction contract
n: In the Interview step, the Architect explains his methodology in translating the plan/design requirements of the proposed project. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.3.2.3 (Interview))

q: A newly-registered architect asks whether the SPP treats the terms “Architect” and “Architectural Firm (AF)” as always legally distinct with no overlap in usage. What does the SPP actually say?
o: AF replaces the term Architect entirely in all SPP documents
Only the Board may determine when the terms are interchangeable, on a case-by-case basis
Architect and AF must never be used interchangeably under any circumstance
Architect and AF may be used interchangeably for some of the succeeding SPP documents
n: The General Definitions expressly state that Architect and Architectural Firm (AF) may be used interchangeably for some of the succeeding SPP documents. (Source: SPP Annex A, General Definitions, Item 7)

q: In the Negotiation step that concludes Comparative Selection, what two things does the Architect explain to the Client?
o: The Scope of Services and the Architect's Fee as prescribed under the Architect's Guidelines
The building permit requirements and zoning restrictions
The jury's composition and the competition rules
The construction schedule and the contractor's bid amount
n: In Negotiation, the Architect explains to the Client the Scope of Services and the Architect's Fee as prescribed under the Architect's Guidelines. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.3.2.6 (Negotiation))

q: Which set of terms does the SPP say may be used interchangeably to refer to the party engaging the Architect's services?
o: Professional, Client, and Board
Client, Owner, and Project Proponent
Sponsor, Contractor, and Constructor
Owner, Builder, and Bidder
n: The General Definitions state that Client, Owner, and Project Proponent may be used interchangeably for the SPP and some of the succeeding SPP documents. (Source: SPP Annex A, General Definitions, Item 9)

q: Which of the following is listed as an advantage of an Architectural Design Competition (ADC)?
o: It eliminates the need for a jury
Opportunities are open only to PRC-registered and licensed Architects or PRC-registered Architectural Firms, giving the Client/Committee a wider range of options
It removes ownership and copyright concerns entirely
It is guaranteed to be faster and cheaper than Direct Selection
n: The listed advantages of an ADC are that opportunities are open only to PRC-registered RLAs/AFs, and that the Client/Committee has a wider range of options. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.3.3.1)

q: According to the SPP General Definitions, what is the relationship between "Bid" and "Tender"?
o: A Bid is submitted only by AFs, while a Tender is submitted only by individual RLAs
A Tender is a formal offer while a Bid is only a preliminary estimate
They mean the same thing
Bid refers to Direct Selection while Tender refers to Comparative Selection
n: Item 11 of the General Definitions states plainly: "Bid and Tender shall mean the same." (Source: SPP Annex A, General Definitions, Item 11)

q: An architect is invited to join a design competition and later suspects the sponsoring 'Client' is actually an unscrupulous party seeking free design services under the guise of a competition. Which legal issue does the SPP specifically flag that architects must stay alert to in this situation?
o: The three-year renewal period of the architect's professional identification card
Ownership and copyright issues under Secs. 20 (4) and 33 of R.A. No. 9266, which must be fully addressed under all architectural competition rules
Whether the Client is registered with the SEC
Whether the competition entry qualifies as a Bid or a Tender
n: The SPP warns that some potentially unscrupulous prospective Clients seek free services under the guise of a design competition, and that ownership and copyright issues under Secs. 20 (4) and 33 of R.A. No. 9266 must be fully addressed under all architectural competition rules. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.3.3.2(c))

q: In the SPP's list of acronyms, what does IAPOA stand for?
o: Integrated Association of Philippine Overseas Architects
International Association of Professional Organization Architects
Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects
Institute for the Advancement of Professional Organizations and Architecture
n: IAPOA is listed in the SPP Acronyms section as the Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. B (Acronyms))

q: In an Architectural Design Competition, who may serve as the Sponsor or Client under the SPP's list of participants?
o: Only a government agency
Only a PRC-registered Architectural Firm
A natural or juridical person
Only a member of the jury
n: Under Participants, the Sponsor or Client may be a natural or juridical person. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.3.3.4(a))

q: TSP, as used in the SPP, stands for what, and which two agencies are involved in issuing its component permits for a foreign architect?
o: Technical Standards Permit — issued by the PRBoA only
Temporary/Special Permit — issued by the Commission (PRC), with a companion work permit from the DoLE
Total Service Package — issued by the DTI and the SEC
Trade Services Permit — issued by the IAPOA
n: TSP means Temporary/Special Permit. As used later in the SPP, a foreign competitor must secure a TSP from the Commission (PRC) and a separate work permit from the Department of Labor and Employment (DoLE). (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. B (Acronyms); Sec. C.3.3.4(b))

q: Who qualifies to serve as a Professional Adviser in an Architectural Design Competition under the SPP?
o: Foreign architects holding a Temporary Special Permit
The Client's in-house legal counsel
Any licensed engineer regardless of IAPOA membership
Philippine-Registered and Licensed Architects (RLAs) who are IAPOA members in good standing
n: The Professional Adviser role is limited to Philippine-Registered and Licensed Architects who are IAPOA members in good standing. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.3.3.4(c))

q: CEC, as listed among the SPP acronyms, stands for what?
o: Codes of Ethical Conduct
Certificate of Employment and Compensation
Construction Ethics Committee
Continuing Education Credits
n: CEC is defined in the SPP acronym list as Codes of Ethical Conduct. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. B (Acronyms))

q: The SPP's Jury composition for an ADC includes an 'Architect' member and a second category of member. What is that second category?
o: A representative of the Securities and Exchange Commission
The Competition Sponsor or Client
A foreign architect holding a TSP
A representative of the Department of Labor and Employment
n: The Jury's listed composition includes (d.1) an Architect who is a member in good standing of the IAPOA, and (d.2) the Competition Sponsor or Client. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.3.3.4(d.1-d.2))

q: According to Section C's Introduction, what determines the most appropriate method of selecting an Architect for a given project?
o: Only the size of the project's budget
The type and complexity of the project
Whether the client is a natural or juridical person
The architect's years of experience alone
n: The Introduction states that the most appropriate method of selecting an Architect will depend on the type and complexity of the project. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.1 (Introduction))

q: Under the 2010 Standards of Professional Practice (SPP), the term "State" refers solely to what?
o: The National Government of the Republic of the Philippines
The Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA)
Any local government unit where a project is located
The Professional Regulation Commission
n: The SPP General Definitions state that "State" shall refer solely to the National Government of the Republic of the Philippines. (Source: SPP Annex A, General Definitions, Item 1)

q: A homeowner planning a relatively small residential project wants to pick an architect quickly, based on the architect's reputation and a friend's recommendation, without running a formal committee process. Which method of selection does this describe?
o: Direct Selection
Architectural Design Competition (ADC)
Pre-qualification
Comparative Selection
n: Direct Selection is used for relatively small projects, where the Client selects the Architect based on reputation, personal/business acquaintance, or recommendation of a friend, former client, or another architect. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.3.1 (Direct Selection))

q: For purposes of the SPP, "Commission" refers only to which body, and under what law was it created?
o: The Professional Regulation Commission (PRC), created under R.A. No. 8981
The Department of Trade and Industry, created under the Corporation Code
The Securities and Exchange Commission, created under R.A. No. 8799
The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture (PRBoA), created under R.A. No. 9266
n: The SPP defines Commission as referring only to the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC), duly created under R.A. No. 8981, The PRC Modernization Act of 2000. (Source: SPP Annex A, General Definitions, Item 3)

q: A government agency forms a selection committee — including representatives from other professions and the construction industry — to evaluate several architects for a large public project. Which selection method is being used, and who typically conducts it?
o: Negotiated procurement under R.A. No. 9184
Comparative Selection, conducted by committees representing institutions, corporations, or public agencies
Architectural Design Competition, conducted only by IAPOA
Direct Selection, conducted solely by the project proponent
n: Comparative Selection may be conducted by committees representing institutions, corporations, or public agencies, and can include representatives from other State-regulated professions and the construction industry. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.3.2)

q: Per the SPP, an "Architect" refers only to a Registered and Licensed Architect (RLA). What must an RLA hold for lawful practice, and how often is it renewed?
o: A valid business permit from the DTI, renewable annually
A Temporary/Special Permit (TSP), renewable every year
A valid certificate of registration and a valid professional identification card, renewable every 3 years
A valid SEC registration, renewable every 5 years
n: An Architect (RLA) is a natural person with a valid certificate of registration and a valid professional identification card representing a renewable 3-year license for the lawful practice of architecture. (Source: SPP Annex A, General Definitions, Item 5)

q: In the Comparative Selection process, what happens during the Pre-qualification step?
o: Architects and/or PRC-registered Architectural Firms submit information on their qualifications and expertise
The architect negotiates the professional fee
The selection committee visits buildings the architects have designed
The Client issues the Terms of Reference
n: Pre-qualification is the step where Architects and/or PRC-registered AFs submit information regarding their qualifications and expertise. (Source: SPP Annex A, Sec. C.3.2.2 (Pre-qualification))

q: An "Architectural Firm (AF)" must be a juridical person duly registered in which way(s) to qualify under the SPP?
o: As a cooperative registered with the Cooperative Development Authority
As any business entity registered with the Department of Labor and Employment
As a natural person with a valid professional identification card from the PRC
As a sole proprietorship with the DTI, or as a partnership/corporation with the SEC and the PRC for architectural practice by RLAs
n: An AF must be a juridical person under Philippine law, registered with the DTI as a sole proprietorship for individual architectural practice, or registered with the SEC and the PRC as a professional partnership, corporation, or group architectural practice by RLAs, subject to full compliance with Sec. 37 of R.A. No. 9266. (Source: SPP Annex A, General Definitions, Item 6)
